items.title: Richard McLean Interview, 1959-05-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...we just stopped at George Gaynos, he said you could play some banjo.

ctx.x: Cindy Gates, yeah. And there's the other two boys, they're very fine guitar players. There's one Trevene and two of them. One is Oivin Trevene and the other one is Curtis Trevene. I taught them. Well there's a few other boys, there's a few others I won't even mention their names because they seem to tell other people, you didn't show me anything. Yeah, sometimes there's a certain jealousy. So when I found out Oivin, I just won't mention the name of them. No, I don't either. And that's true.

A lot of people have told me how wonderful you were on banjo, like Professor Mineta, and we just stopped at George Gaynos, he said you could play some banjo. They all talk about it, so I wish I could have heard you sometime. I never always think of you as a bass player. Which instrument do you really enjoy most, bass or banjo, guitar?
I'll tell you, I'll tell you. Player of that, maybe. I don't know why I didn't have a bass long years ago because I always did like the bass.
